purpose: How a travel advisor turns booked trips into money that actually arrives and clients who actually come back - reading each supplier's commissionable base and payment trigger as a mechanism rather than a remembered rate, recording and reconciling every expected commission through the host or direct payout path, chasing shortfalls and absorbing cancellation clawbacks without wrecking cash flow, capturing planning fees under written engagement terms, offering travel-protection add-ons only inside a verified licensing requirement class and only on honest fit, and running the post-trip, anniversary and referral cadence that gives a low-frequency vertical its recurrence and gives the client book whatever value it has.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the practice is a small leisure-focused travel advisory business - a solo advisor or a handful of independent contractors - selling published supplier product rather than buying inventory at net as a tour operator or wholesaler

every commission rate, host split, bonus tier, planning-fee level, add-on commission and client-book multiple named here is a mechanism to be read out of a specific contract, supplier schedule or negotiated deal and verified per booking; none of them is carried as a remembered fact

travel-protection selling and the acts of describing, recommending or interpreting coverage sit inside licensing, appointment and disclosure obligation classes that differ by state, province and country and change over time; this knowledge base names the class and the verification act and never asserts what a specific jurisdiction currently requires
clients in this vertical can compare and book online at any moment and talk to each other, so honest expectation-setting and disclosure are commercial mechanics as well as compliance duties
recurrence here is behavioural rather than contractual - there is no subscription, so the next booking is earned by follow-up, records and trust rather than billed automatically
this is educational operating knowledge for running the practice, not personalized financial, tax, legal, medical or insurance advice for any advisor or client
exclusions: choosing between host-agency affiliation and independent accreditation, comparing hosts or consortia, and deciding whether to register or how the practice is structured - the agency-models and niche KB owns those decisions and hands this KB the resulting contract terms

niche selection, positioning, credentialing, and the design decision of whether to charge planning fees at all and at what level - agency-models KB territory; this KB only executes and measures the fee that decision produced

client discovery interviews, itinerary design, supplier selection and preferred-program choice, reservation mechanics, document preparation, and in-trip disruption advocacy - the trip-design and supplier-management KB owns the delivery craft that this KB monetizes and follows up on
quality control during the trip itself and service recovery while the client is travelling - trip-design and supplier-management KB territory; this KB starts at the welcome-home contact

naming specific host agencies, consortia, suppliers, insurers or protection products, and quoting any commission rate, split, bonus tier, fee amount, claim-window length or book-value multiple as a fact

jurisdiction-specific legal conclusions about seller-of-travel registration, insurance producer licensing, appointment or trust-account rules - these appear only as obligation classes to verify with the regulator, the insurer and the host

interpreting policy wording, assessing whether a specific traveller's circumstances are covered, predicting or adjudicating a claim outcome, or recommending a specific insurance product to a specific person

steering a client toward whichever supplier or protection product pays the advisor best while concealing that it pays - excluded as a practice, not a technique; compensation-driven recommendation without disclosure is treated here only as a failure mode
personalized financial, tax, legal, medical or insurance advice to any advisor or client, and any tax treatment of commission or fee income

competency_questions.question: When is a commission actually earned versus actually paid on a booking, and how do I plan a month around that gap?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOKED_VS_TRAVELED_TIMING separates the work, earning and payment events and derives an expected pay window per booking, and CASHFLOW_RUNWAY_MANAGEMENT converts those windows into a pipeline the practice can live on

competency_questions.question: For the booking in front of me, which part of the price is commissionable and what would void the commission entirely?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_TERMS_READOUT names the document that defines the commissionable base for that supplier and product and lists the conditions that void or reduce it, without quoting a rate as fact

competency_questions.question: What has to be written down at the moment of booking so an unpaid commission can still be proved months after the trip?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_EXPECTATION_RECORD lists the fields and evidence attachments of the expectation row and HOST_STATEMENT_AND_SPLIT states which of them the payout path will need to match on

competency_questions.question: How do I reconcile a host or supplier statement against what I expected, and how do I classify a variance?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMMISSION_RECONCILIATION gives the match rule and the variance classes (not yet due, short base, wrong split tier, paid on another booking, genuinely missing) and HOST_STATEMENT_AND_SPLIT explains how the split is applied per line

competency_questions.question: A commission is late or short - what is the escalation ladder, and when do I stop chasing it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: UNPAID_COMMISSION_CHASE specifies the evidence pack, the escalation ladder bounded by the supplier's own stated claim window, and the write-off decision that weighs recovery against advisor hours

competency_questions.question: What happens to revenue I have already counted when a trip cancels, downgrades or is refunded after payment?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CANCELLATION_AND_CLAWBACK describes reversal, recall and offset as mechanisms and states which revenue lines can survive a cancellation, and CASHFLOW_RUNWAY_MANAGEMENT sizes a reserve against that exposure

competency_questions.question: How do I collect a planning fee so that it survives a cancellation, a direct booking and an awkward conversation?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLANNING_FEE_CAPTURE states the pre-work collection sequence, the written scope of what the fee buys and does not buy, the refund or credit policy, and the handling of waiver and direct-booking requests

competency_questions.question: Which kinds of engagement actually pay for the hours they consume, and which do I stop taking?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EFFORT_TO_REALIZED_REVENUE compares hours consumed against revenue actually received per engagement class and produces a qualitative band, never an invented benchmark margin

competency_questions.question: What must I verify before I offer travel protection at all, and what am I allowed to say about it once I do?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROTECTION_REQUIREMENT_CLASS names the licensing, appointment and disclosure obligation classes and the verification act, and COVERAGE_FIT_CONVERSATION draws the describe-versus-advise line inside that class

competency_questions.question: How do I make sure every client is offered protection without pressuring anyone, and how do I prove later what was offered?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROTECTION_OFFER_DISCIPLINE fixes the offer point and the dated offer-and-decision record, and ETHICAL_ADDON_SELLING_RULE bounds the offer with the no-fear-selling, disclosure and vulnerable-client rules

competency_questions.question: A client is filing a claim or has been denied - what is my role, and what did I promise them at the point of sale?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLAIM_TIME_ROLE limits the advisor to document custodian and facilitator with the insurer deciding, and COVERAGE_FIT_CONVERSATION shows the at-sale language that set that expectation

competency_questions.question: What happens in the weeks after the client comes home that turns one trip into the next one?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_TRIP_DEBRIEF defines the welcome-home contact and what it harvests, and ANNIVERSARY_AND_REBOOK_CADENCE times the next contact against the client's own planning window

competency_questions.question: How do I ask for referrals and reviews without turning a warm relationship into a transaction or buying an endorsement?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERRAL_ENGINE gives the ask, the forwardable handoff and the loop-closing thank-you, and ETHICAL_ADDON_SELLING_RULE forbids undisclosed incentives and traded endorsements

competency_questions.question: What makes a client base worth anything in a vertical with no subscription, and what of it can actually transfer to anyone else?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_VALUE_AND_CONTINUITY names the value drivers, the concentration risk and the contract terms that decide portability while treating any multiple as a negotiated mechanism, supported by CLIENT_RECORD_AND_PREFERENCE_ASSET and DORMANCY_AND_REACTIVATION

glossary.definition: The slice of a booking's price that a given supplier actually pays commission on, defined in that supplier's own agency terms; taxes, port charges, resort fees, gratuities, insurance premiums and air portions are commonly carved out in ways that differ by supplier and product, so the base is read per booking rather than assumed.

The event a supplier's schedule names as the point commission becomes payable - most commonly after travel is completed or after departure, sometimes at final payment and occasionally at deposit; it is what turns a booking date into an expected pay window.

A supplier's recovery of commission it has already paid, typically applied as an offset against a later statement, after a booking cancels, is refunded, is downgraded or is repriced; it is the reason pre-travel payments are treated as provisional.

The supplier's record of which agency owns a booking and is therefore paid on it; it can be lost or moved when a client books or rebooks directly, when a reservation is transferred, or when a booking is repriced through another channel.

The period a supplier or host states for submitting a missing-commission claim with supporting evidence; the length is set in each supplier's own terms, so the window is looked up and diarized per supplier rather than remembered as one number.

An insurance or assistance product offered alongside a trip whose benefit categories, exclusions and timing conditions are defined by the insurer's own documents; what an advisor may say about one depends on the licensing and appointment class that applies to them.

A review window many protection plans provide during which the purchaser can cancel for a refund of premium; a cancellation inside it typically reverses the advisor's add-on commission, which is why that revenue line stays provisional until the window closes.

A mechanism common in protection plans that examines a defined period of medical history before purchase and often ties any waiver of that exclusion to buying within a defined number of days of the initial trip payment; the specific periods and conditions live in the plan documents, never in the advisor's summary.

The dated note showing that protection was offered to a client, what product family was described, and what the client decided; it is the evidence that protects the client from being quietly skipped and the advisor from a later dispute about what was said.

The practice's accumulated client base and the records, preferences, trip histories and referral relationships attached to it; what it is worth depends on documentation, repeat and referral behaviour, revenue concentration and whether the governing contracts permit any of it to transfer.

nodes.definition: Draw the single map of where this practice's money comes from and when each stream becomes real: supplier commission on booked travel, client-paid planning or service fees, commission on travel-protection and other add-ons, and the supplier or consortium bonus and override programs that sit on top of base commission when volume or preferred-program conditions are met. The frame's whole job is to separate three moments that a new advisor collapses into one - the moment the work is done, the moment the revenue is earned, and the moment the cash arrives - and to force every stream to carry its own trigger for each. It also fixes the honesty rule the rest of this subdomain runs on: no rate, split, bonus tier or fee level is a number the advisor carries in their head, because each one exists as a term in a specific contract, supplier agency schedule or host plan document and is read out per booking. The unit is complete when the advisor can name every revenue stream the practice has, the document that defines it, the event that earns it, the event that pays it, and the person or entity that pays.

included: the four revenue streams and the document defining each
the earning event and the payment event for each stream
the read-it-per-deal rule that bars remembered rates
excluded: whether to charge planning fees and at what level - the agency-models KB's fee-model design
quoting trip prices to clients
tax treatment of the income

pros.claim: Separating earned revenue from arrived cash stops an advisor spending money that has not landed
pros.example: a heavy booking season for next summer's sailings that produces almost nothing in the bank until those sailings actually happen

pros.claim: Naming the defining document per stream makes every later dispute a lookup instead of an argument
pros.example: a bonus that never appeared being traced to the program's stated qualifying conditions rather than debated from memory

cons.claim: A revenue map is a snapshot and quietly goes stale as supplier schedules and host plans change
cons.example: a supplier revising what counts as its commissionable base mid-year while the advisor still forecasts on last year's assumption

failure_modes: treating gross booking volume as if it were income
carrying a remembered commission rate instead of reading the current schedule
leaving add-on and bonus revenue off the map so nobody ever reconciles it
mixing client money in transit with practice revenue in the same mental account
acceptance_tests: every revenue stream the practice has is listed with its defining document, its earning event, its payment event and its payer
no rate, split or fee level appears in the map as a remembered figure rather than a pointer to a document
revisit_triggers: a host or supplier restates its commission, split or bonus schedule
the practice introduces a new fee type or add-on revenue line
an unexplained revenue line appears on a statement

base.update_signal: a new revenue stream is added to the practice or a host or supplier restates the schedule that defines an existing one

nodes.definition: For the specific supplier and product in hand, establish what commission is actually payable on before treating any of it as revenue. That means locating the commissionable base in the supplier's own agency terms - the cruise fare separate from port charges, taxes and gratuities, the room rate separate from resort fees and local taxes, the land portion separate from air, the package price separate from the insurance premium inside it - and noting whether the applicable rate is a base rate, a promotional or group rate with different terms, or a preferred-program rate that only applies while a condition holds. Equally important are the void and reduction conditions: bookings repriced or rebooked through the supplier's own call centre, reservations moved to another agency, group blocks converted to individual bookings, refundable components cancelled, and any rule about agency of record. The advisor also records where the answer came from, because the same word means different things across two suppliers and next season's schedule may not match this one. The unit is done when the advisor can state, for this booking, the base, the source document, and at least one condition that would remove the commission entirely.

included: locating the commissionable base per supplier and product
identifying void, reduction and agency-of-record conditions
recording the source document for the read
excluded: choosing which supplier to book - trip-design and supplier-management KB
negotiating rates or preferred-program status
asserting any rate as a fixed figure

pros.claim: Reading the base per booking prevents a pipeline full of revenue that was never payable
pros.example: counting the whole package price on a booking where taxes, port charges and the insurance premium are a large non-commissionable slice

pros.claim: Knowing the void conditions changes how the advisor handles ordinary client requests
pros.example: a client calling the supplier directly to change a cabin and unknowingly moving the booking out of the advisor's agency of record

cons.claim: Reading terms per supplier per product is slow and is the first discipline abandoned in a busy season
cons.example: a peak-season booking taken on a half-remembered rate because six other clients are waiting

cons.claim: Terms documents are written for the supplier's protection and often leave real cases ambiguous
cons.example: a mixed itinerary where it is genuinely unclear whether a transfer sits inside the commissionable land portion

failure_modes: assuming one supplier's definition of the commissionable base applies to another
missing that a promotional or group fare carries different agency terms than the published one
failing to notice that a client's direct contact with the supplier moved the agency of record
reading the terms once at sign-up and never again
acceptance_tests: for a sample booking the advisor can point to the clause and document that define the commissionable base
at least one condition that would void or reduce commission on that booking is named and recorded on the booking file
revisit_triggers: a supplier republishes its agency or commission terms
a booking is modified, repriced, rebooked or moved to a promotional fare
a statement shows a payment computed on a smaller base than expected

base.update_signal: a supplier republishes agency terms or a reconciled payment lands on a different base than the one recorded at booking

nodes.definition: Internalize and operationalize the structural fact of this vertical: the advisor's work is front-loaded into planning, booking and document preparation, while most supplier commission is only payable after the travel happens, with the exact trigger - after return, after departure, at final payment, occasionally at deposit - stated in each supplier's own schedule and in the host's payout terms. The consequences run through everything else. A month's income reflects trips taken, not trips sold. A long-lead booking parks its revenue a season or more into the future. A record booking week can sit alongside an empty bank account, which is exactly when advisors quit. And anything that stops the trip happening removes revenue that already felt earned. Operationally the unit converts each booking into an expected pay window derived from travel dates plus the supplier's stated trigger plus the host's payout run, and forces the practice to report booked volume and traveled-and-received revenue as two separate lines that are never added together.

included: the work, earning and payment events and the gap between them
deriving an expected pay window per booking from travel dates and the stated trigger
reporting booked and traveled-and-received as separate lines
excluded: the cash decisions taken because of the gap - those belong to the runway unit
supplier payment disputes
personal budgeting advice

pros.claim: An expected pay window per booking turns a vague hope into a datable forecast row
pros.example: a shoulder-season booking made now being placed in the correct post-travel window instead of this quarter's expectations

pros.claim: Reporting booked and received separately removes the most common morale trap in a new practice
pros.example: an advisor with a strong sales month understanding why the bank balance has not moved yet, instead of concluding the business does not work

cons.claim: A forecast built on travel dates is only as good as the trip happening, so one cancellation invalidates a whole row
cons.example: a family reunion cruise falling apart and taking a forecast month's largest line with it

cons.claim: Long-lead bookings make the pipeline look healthy while doing nothing for the current quarter
cons.example: a year-out expedition booking that flatters the pipeline and pays nothing in the season the advisor needs it

failure_modes: recognizing revenue at booking and being surprised by the drought that follows
assuming every supplier pays on the same trigger
forgetting the host's own payout run adds a lag after the supplier pays
planning personal spending on booked volume
acceptance_tests: each open booking carries an expected pay window derived from its travel dates and the supplier's stated payment trigger
the practice's income view shows booked volume and traveled-and-received revenue as separate, non-additive lines
revisit_triggers: a supplier or host changes its payment trigger or payout schedule
the practice's product mix shifts toward longer-lead or shorter-lead travel

base.update_signal: a supplier or host restates when commission becomes payable, or the practice's typical booking-to-travel lead time changes materially

nodes.definition: Open one ledger row per booking at the moment the booking is made, not when money is expected, because the payment arrives months later as a line on somebody else's statement and the trip will have faded from memory by then. The row carries the client and travelling names as the supplier holds them, the supplier and its confirmation or reservation number, the agency identifier the booking was made under, travel dates, the commissionable base as actually read, the rate source pointer, the expected gross before any split, the payout path this booking will travel, the expected pay window, and any condition flagged as a risk to the payment. Attached to it sits the evidence pack the advisor would need to prove the claim later: the confirmation, the supplier invoice showing the agency, and the payment record. Add-on protection sales get their own row with their own trigger rather than being folded into the trip. The unit is complete when a row can be reconstructed and defended by someone who has no memory of the trip at all.

included: the fields and evidence attachments of the per-booking expectation row
separate rows for add-on and bonus-eligible revenue
flagging conditions that threaten the payment
excluded: the booking and documentation workflow itself - trip-design and supplier-management KB
storing client payment card data, which stays in the supplier's own channel
accounting or bookkeeping treatment

pros.claim: A row opened at booking is the only version of the facts that exists while they are still fresh
pros.example: a shortfall queried eight months later answered instantly from the recorded base and the attached invoice

pros.claim: Separate rows for add-ons make an otherwise invisible revenue line reconcilable
pros.example: a protection plan sold months before departure whose commission would otherwise never be missed if it never arrived

cons.claim: The discipline costs minutes on every booking and pays back only when something goes wrong
cons.example: an advisor skipping the row on a simple hotel booking that later turns out to be the one that was never paid

cons.claim: A record that duplicates supplier data can drift out of step with the supplier's own file
cons.example: a name or date changed with the supplier after booking and never updated on the expectation row

failure_modes: recording an amount without recording the base and the rate source that produced it
logging the trip but not the add-on sale
keeping the evidence in an email thread that is never attached to the row
letting client-identifying detail accumulate beyond what the practice's privacy terms cover
acceptance_tests: a randomly chosen open row contains payer, supplier, confirmation number, agency identifier, travel dates, base, rate source, expected gross, payout path and expected pay window
the evidence pack attached to that row is sufficient to file a missing-commission claim without contacting the client
revisit_triggers: a booking is amended, rebooked or transferred
a statement cannot be matched to any open row
the host changes the identifiers it reports payments under

base.update_signal: a reconciliation cycle finds payments that cannot be matched to rows, or the host changes its reporting identifiers

nodes.definition: Trace how the money physically reaches the advisor and learn to read the document it arrives with. In a hosted practice the supplier pays the host, the host applies the split or plan terms written into the independent contractor agreement, and the advisor is paid on the host's own payout run, which adds its own lag; an independently accredited practice is paid by suppliers directly and carries the matching work itself. The mechanics to master are which identifier each supplier reports the payment under, how the host's statement lines are labelled, whether the split is applied per line and at what tier or plan level the advisor currently sits, how the host handles a payment it cannot match to an advisor, what happens to a payment that arrives after an advisor leaves, and what recourse and timeline the agreement gives when a line is wrong. All of it is read out of the actual agreement and the actual statement - the split, tier thresholds and any plan fees are contract terms, never assumed figures, and they can change at renewal.

included: the supplier-to-host-to-advisor payout path and its lags
reading statement lines and identifiers
how and where the split or plan terms are applied per line
excluded: choosing or comparing a host agency or negotiating the split - agency-models KB
the reconciliation decision itself
asserting any split percentage or plan fee as fact

pros.claim: Knowing which identifier a payment will arrive under makes matching mechanical rather than forensic
pros.example: a supplier reporting under the lead traveller's surname while the advisor's row is filed under the household name, resolved once and then always

pros.claim: Knowing the agreement's recourse path turns a wrong statement line into a defined request
pros.example: a line paid at the wrong tier queried through the host's stated dispute channel with the tier clause cited

cons.claim: The advisor sees the supplier's payment only through the host's presentation of it
cons.example: a statement that shows a net figure without the base and rate the supplier actually used

cons.claim: Statement formats and plan terms change at the host's discretion, invalidating a settled routine
cons.example: a reformatted statement that no longer carries the reference field the advisor's matching depended on

failure_modes: matching a statement line by amount alone
assuming the split shown last quarter still applies after a plan or tier change
ignoring the host payout lag when forecasting cash
never reading the agreement's dispute clause until there is a dispute
acceptance_tests: the advisor can trace one paid booking from supplier payment through the host statement line to the amount received, naming where the split was applied
the current plan or tier and the agreement clause defining it are recorded rather than remembered
revisit_triggers: the host changes statement format, payout schedule, plan structure or tier thresholds
the advisor's plan or volume tier changes
the affiliation itself changes

base.update_signal: the host restates its statement format, payout schedule or plan and tier structure, or the practice changes affiliation

nodes.definition: Run a repeating close in which every payment received is matched to an open expectation row and every open row is given a status, so the practice always knows what is owed to it. Matching uses traveller name, supplier, confirmation number and travel dates together rather than amount alone, because amounts collide and lump payments hide several bookings. Each unmatched or short line is then classified rather than merely noticed: not yet due against its expected pay window, short because the base differed from the one recorded, short because a different split tier or plan term was applied, paid against another booking or another period, offset by a recall on a cancelled trip, or genuinely missing. Open rows are aged against their expected pay windows and carry an escalation date derived from the supplier's own stated claim window. The close ends with every row matched, aged, escalated or written off with a reason - never simply left open - and its by-product is a running picture of which suppliers pay cleanly and which cost the practice hours.

included: the match rule and the variance classification
ageing open rows against expected pay windows and claim windows
the close discipline that leaves no row unstatused
excluded: the escalation conversation itself
bookkeeping, tax or financial-statement preparation
supplier selection decisions

pros.claim: Classifying a variance instead of just seeing it tells the advisor whether to wait, query or claim
pros.example: a short payment traced to a different tier being routed to the host rather than chased at the supplier

pros.claim: Ageing rows converts a vague sense of being underpaid into a dated queue
pros.example: three rows past their expected windows surfacing in the same close and being escalated in one sitting

cons.claim: A monthly close is real unbillable time that competes with selling
cons.example: an afternoon spent matching statement lines in a month when three clients are mid-design

cons.claim: Aggressive matching can close a row that was actually paid against a different booking, hiding a real shortfall
cons.example: a coincidental amount match that marks one row settled while the genuinely unpaid one looks fine

failure_modes: matching by amount alone
treating unmatched as missing without checking the expected window first
letting the close slip during peak season and losing claim windows
closing rows with no reason recorded
acceptance_tests: after a close, every open row carries a status of matched, not yet due, queried, escalated or written off with a reason
no row is marked matched on amount alone without a name, confirmation or travel-date agreement
revisit_triggers: a supplier's payments start arriving in a new format or cadence
the unmatched pile grows across consecutive closes
a written-off row is later paid

base.update_signal: the unmatched or short-paid share of rows changes materially across consecutive closes

nodes.definition: Turn an aged row into a filed claim, and know when to stop. The claim starts as an evidence pack - confirmation number, supplier invoice showing the agency, guest names as travelled, travel dates completed, the agency identifier, and the expectation row's recorded base - assembled once and reused at every rung. The ladder runs from the host's own commission-support channel where one exists, to the supplier's agency commission desk, to the business development or sales contact who owns the relationship, each rung with a dated note and each bounded by the claim window the supplier itself states, which is looked up per supplier rather than assumed. Tone matters commercially: the same person is a supplier the practice wants to book again next season, so the claim is a documented request, not a grievance. The write-off decision weighs the amount and the hours the chase will take against the same hours spent on a paying client, and every write-off is still logged, because a supplier that repeatedly short-pays is telling the practice something about whether to keep selling it.

included: the reusable evidence pack
the escalation ladder bounded by the supplier's stated claim window
the write-off decision and its logging as supplier-performance evidence
excluded: legal action or debt collection
renegotiating commercial terms - agency-models KB
asserting how long any supplier's claim window is

pros.claim: A prepared evidence pack makes a claim a five-minute act instead of an afternoon of archaeology
pros.example: a completed-travel claim filed from the row's attachments without reopening the client's file

pros.claim: Logging write-offs converts individually trivial losses into a supplier-selection signal
pros.example: three small unpaid rows from the same supplier in a season prompting a review of whether it stays in rotation

cons.claim: Chasing consumes exactly the hours that would otherwise earn new revenue
cons.example: half a day spent recovering a small hotel commission that a single client conversation would have out-earned

cons.claim: Persistent escalation can strain a supplier relationship the practice depends on for client outcomes
cons.example: a repeatedly escalated small claim souring the contact the advisor needs for a client's upgrade request

failure_modes: discovering the claim window has closed
filing without the invoice that proves the agency booked it
chasing every trivial amount with the same intensity as a large one
letting frustration into a message that the supplier files permanently
acceptance_tests: each escalated row shows a dated ladder of contacts and the evidence pack that was sent
each closed row shows either recovery or a logged write-off reason attributed to a supplier
revisit_triggers: a supplier changes its commission-support channel or claim terms
the same supplier produces repeat shortfalls
a claim succeeds through a path not previously used

base.update_signal: a supplier changes its claim channel or window, or recovery outcomes shift consistently for a supplier

nodes.definition: Handle the revenue side of trips that do not happen as sold. Cancellations before travel simply remove expected commission; refunds, downgrades and repricings after travel or after payment can trigger a recall in which the supplier recovers commission already paid, usually as an offset against a later statement, and a protection plan cancelled inside its free-look window reverses its own add-on commission the same way. The practice's real exposure is the difference between what it has recognized and what would survive: a planning fee collected under written engagement terms for work already performed can survive a cancellation if those terms say so, while supplier commission generally cannot. The unit's discipline is to mark any commission received before travel completes as provisional, to keep the expectation row open until the reversal risk has passed, to check whether a cancelled booking's rebooking preserves the agency of record, and to record every reversal against the row it came from so the pattern is visible rather than experienced as random statement shrinkage.

included: reversal, recall and offset as mechanisms
which revenue lines can survive a cancellation and under what document
marking pre-travel receipts provisional until the risk passes
excluded: handling the client's cancellation and rebooking itself - trip-design KB
advising a client whether to claim on their protection plan
any statement about what a specific supplier's penalty schedule is

pros.claim: Treating pre-travel receipts as provisional stops the practice spending money it may have to give back
pros.example: a deposit-paid commission held aside until the sailing actually departs rather than counted as the month's income

pros.claim: Recording reversals against their rows makes a shrinking statement explainable instead of alarming
pros.example: a statement that is lighter than expected being traced immediately to two offsets from a cancelled group

cons.claim: Holding revenue as provisional understates income for months and can make a healthy practice look weak
cons.example: a strong season that reports conservatively because most of its commission is still reversible

cons.claim: Reversal exposure is concentrated in exactly the large bookings the practice most wants
cons.example: one multi-cabin family booking whose collapse removes more than a month of ordinary bookings

failure_modes: spending pre-travel commission as though travel had happened
closing an expectation row before the reversal window has passed
not noticing an offset because it appears as a smaller net line rather than a labelled reversal
assuming a planning fee is refundable or non-refundable without reading the engagement terms that were actually issued
acceptance_tests: commission received before travel completes is flagged provisional and excluded from the practice's spendable figure
every reversal or offset on a statement is matched back to the booking that produced it
revisit_triggers: a supplier changes how it handles recalls or presents offsets
a season produces an unusual concentration of cancellations
the practice's mix shifts toward products with longer penalty ladders

base.update_signal: an unusual volume of reversals appears in a period, or a supplier changes how recalls are applied and presented

nodes.definition: Run the practice across the structural gap between doing the work and being paid for it. The instrument is a three-state pipeline view - booked but not yet travelled, travelled but not yet paid, and received - refreshed at each close so the advisor can see how much of the next months' cash is already determined and how much still has to be sold. Because the calendar that matters is travel dates rather than booking dates, seasonality lands differently than it feels: the quiet selling months may pay well and the busiest selling weeks may pay nothing for two seasons. On top of that sits a reserve sized in qualitative terms against the practice's own reversal exposure and its thinnest historical stretch, and a draw discipline that pays the advisor from received-and-non-reversible revenue rather than from statements that are still provisional. The levers available are real but limited: fee capture timing pulls some revenue forward, product and lead-time mix changes the shape of the curve, and declining chronically underwater work frees the hours that produce revenue at all. Sizing is judgement against the practice's own history; no benchmark figure applies.

included: the booked, travelled and received pipeline view
reserve sizing against reversal exposure and thin stretches as a qualitative judgement
the levers that reshape the cash curve
excluded: borrowing, credit or investment decisions and any personalized financial advice
bookkeeping and tax
pricing or fee-level design - agency-models KB

pros.claim: A three-state pipeline shows how much of the coming quarter is already sold and how much is still hope
pros.example: an advisor seeing that most of next quarter's cash sits in trips already travelling and choosing to invest that time in acquisition

pros.claim: Paying the advisor only from non-reversible received revenue prevents a personal cash crisis caused by a business reversal
pros.example: a cancelled group producing an offset that lands harmlessly because it was never drawn against

cons.claim: Holding a reserve in a practice with thin margins can feel like starving the business of the marketing it needs
cons.example: a reserve held through a slow winter while a promising destination campaign is postponed

cons.claim: The pipeline view is only as honest as the expectation rows behind it, so its confidence is borrowed
cons.example: a healthy-looking quarter resting on rows whose commissionable base was never verified

failure_modes: drawing personal income from provisional commission
planning the year on booking seasonality instead of travel seasonality
carrying no reserve in a business whose revenue can be recalled
cutting the reserve to fund work that the margin review already showed is underwater
acceptance_tests: the pipeline separates booked, travelled-not-paid and received, and the practice's spendable figure counts only the last of the three net of provisional lines
a stated reserve intention exists and is expressed against the practice's own reversal exposure and thin-season history
revisit_triggers: a season lands materially away from the pipeline's expectation
reversal exposure rises after a run of cancellations
the product mix or typical lead time shifts

base.update_signal: actual receipts diverge materially from the pipeline forecast for a period, or reversal exposure changes shape

nodes.definition: Execute the fee decision the practice has already made, which is a different skill from designing it. Capture means the fee is agreed and collected before design work starts, under written engagement terms that state plainly what the fee buys - discovery, research, itinerary design, a defined number of revisions, booking and document management, in-trip support - and what it does not buy, that it is payment for advisory work rather than a markup on the trip, and whether it is credited against a booking, non-refundable, or partly both. It travels on a payment rail the practice controls with a receipt issued, and it is recorded as its own revenue line, because unlike commission it is earned when the work is done rather than when someone travels. The hard part is the awkward cases: a client asking for the fee to be waived, a client who pays the fee and then books directly, a client who cancels mid-design, and a referred prospect who did not know a fee existed. Each is answered from the terms the client already signed rather than improvised in the moment.

included: pre-work collection sequence and written scope of the engagement
refund, credit and cancellation policy as issued to the client
handling waiver, direct-booking and mid-design cancellation requests
excluded: whether to charge a fee and at what level, and the client-alignment argument for fee models - agency-models KB
quoting or discounting trip prices
any statement of a market-typical fee amount

pros.claim: A fee collected before design work makes the advisor's time the thing being paid for, which is what it actually is
pros.example: a multi-week itinerary build that starts only after the engagement is signed and the fee has cleared

pros.claim: Written scope converts the most common client conflicts into a reference rather than a negotiation
pros.example: a fifth round of revisions answered by the revision clause the client accepted at the start

cons.claim: Asking for money before producing anything loses some prospects, especially referrals expecting free advice
cons.example: a referred enquirer who assumed the service was free because the referrer never mentioned the fee

cons.claim: A fee sets a service expectation the practice must then honour under time pressure
cons.example: a fee-paying client expecting same-day responses during a week the advisor is managing a disruption for someone else

failure_modes: starting design work on a verbal promise of payment
issuing terms that never state the refund or credit position
waiving the fee case by case until it means nothing
positioning the fee as a discount on the trip rather than payment for advice
acceptance_tests: no design work begins before signed engagement terms and a cleared fee, or a recorded, deliberate exception
the issued terms state what the fee buys, what it excludes and the refund or credit position, and the client has a receipt
revisit_triggers: clients repeatedly push back at the same point in the terms
a mid-design cancellation exposes an unclear clause
the practice changes what is included in the service

base.update_signal: clients consistently object at one clause, or a cancellation or direct-booking case exposes terms that do not answer it

nodes.definition: Compare, per engagement and then per class of engagement, the hours actually consumed against the revenue that actually arrived. Hours include the invisible ones: discovery calls, research on a destination never booked, itinerary revisions, supplier chasing, document assembly, in-trip messages across time zones, and the post-trip follow-up. Revenue means received and non-reversible commission after the split, plus fees collected, plus add-on commission - not booking value and not expected commission. The output is deliberately a qualitative ranking rather than a computed margin: which trip types, supplier categories and client patterns reliably pay for the time they take, which are break-even but strategically worth keeping because they feed referrals, and which are chronically underwater. That ranking is what makes the practice's hardest decisions decidable - who to invite back through the cadence, which enquiries to decline or redirect, where a fee has to carry work that commission never will. No industry benchmark is imported; the comparison is against the practice's own history and the advisor's own capacity.

included: capturing true hours including unbilled and post-trip time
measuring against received non-reversible revenue
the qualitative ranking of engagement classes and the decline decision it supports
excluded: setting fee levels or rate cards - agency-models KB
any benchmark margin or industry-average figure
judging suppliers on service quality rather than economics - trip-design KB

pros.claim: Counting the invisible hours exposes work that felt profitable and never was
pros.example: a complex multi-country itinerary with many revisions that realized less than a repeat cruise booking taking a fraction of the time

pros.claim: A ranking makes declining work a business decision rather than a personal rejection
pros.example: an enquiry type the practice can honestly redirect because the record shows it never pays for its hours

cons.claim: Time tracking is tedious and the first thing to lapse, which biases the sample toward remembered painful cases
cons.example: only the frustrating engagements getting logged, making the average look worse than it is

cons.claim: Pure economics undervalues engagements whose real return is the referrals they generate
cons.example: a low-value honeymoon booking whose family produces several later trips

failure_modes: measuring against booking value instead of received revenue
excluding post-trip and support time from the hours
declining a class of work on one bad case
importing an outside benchmark instead of comparing with the practice's own record
acceptance_tests: each reviewed engagement shows hours including support and post-trip time against received, non-reversible revenue
engagement classes are ranked into pays-for-itself, strategic break-even and chronically underwater with the evidence attached
revisit_triggers: the practice adds a new trip type or client segment
a class ranked underwater changes after a fee or scope change
capacity changes because of hours available or staffing

base.update_signal: a full cycle of tracked engagements changes the ranking of a trip type, or capacity assumptions change

nodes.definition: Before a single protection plan is presented, establish which obligation classes apply to this advisor in this jurisdiction and under this affiliation. The classes to identify and verify are: whether selling or soliciting travel insurance requires a producer or limited-lines licence class, whether the advisor must be appointed by the insurer or may operate under the host's or a program's licence, how seller-of-travel registration classes interact with offering insurance, what the applicable rules define as merely describing a product versus soliciting, recommending or advising on it, what must be disclosed about the advisor's compensation, and what records must be kept and for how long. The verification act is the point of the unit: confirm current requirements with the relevant regulator and with the host and insurer rather than with a peer, a social-media thread or a memory of last year, and re-verify at renewal and on any change of state, residence or affiliation. Requirements differ by state, province and country and change; nothing here states what any jurisdiction currently requires. If the class cannot be confirmed, the practice books the travel and refers the client to a licensed source instead of offering.

included: naming the licensing, appointment, disclosure and record-keeping classes that may apply
the verification act with regulator, insurer and host, and its cadence
the fallback of booking travel only and referring the client to a licensed source
excluded: stating what any jurisdiction requires, what a licence is called, or what any threshold or exemption is
the registration and entity decisions of the practice - agency-models KB
legal advice of any kind

pros.claim: Verifying the class before offering keeps a revenue line from being built on ground that has to be abandoned
pros.example: an add-on script and client expectation created before discovering that the offer route required an appointment the advisor did not hold

pros.claim: Knowing where describing ends and advising begins gives the advisor a usable sentence under pressure
pros.example: a client pressing for a coverage opinion and receiving a clear referral to the insurer instead of an improvised answer

cons.claim: Verification is slow, involves several bodies, and must be repeated rather than done once
cons.example: a practice that adds clients in another state having to re-check before offering there

cons.claim: The conservative line can cost real revenue and leave clients less protected in the meantime
cons.example: declining to present any plan while a class is unconfirmed, and a client travelling with no protection at all

failure_modes: taking a peer's or a forum's word for what is required
assuming the host's licence covers the advisor without confirming the arrangement in writing
verifying once at start-up and never at renewal or after moving
offering while the class is unresolved because the sale is in front of you
acceptance_tests: the applicable obligation classes are written down with the body that confirmed each and the date of confirmation
no protection product is presented to a client before that record exists, and the fallback referral path is documented
revisit_triggers: a licence, appointment or registration renewal falls due
the practice, the advisor's residence or the client base moves into another jurisdiction
the host or insurer changes the arrangement under which offers are made

base.update_signal: a regulator, insurer or host restates the requirements, or the practice's jurisdictional footprint changes

nodes.definition: Make the protection offer a fixed part of the booking process rather than a judgement call about who looks like a buyer, and record what happened. The offer sits at a defined point in the sequence - typically at or before deposit, because several benefit classes in these products carry purchase-timing conditions relative to the initial trip payment, and again at final payment where the plan permits - and it goes to every client, including the ones an advisor assumes will decline. What is recorded is dated and specific: that protection was offered, which product family was described, what materials were provided, and what the client decided, in the client's own words where possible. The record protects the client, who never gets quietly skipped because of an assumption about their budget, and it protects the advisor when a disruption later prompts the question of what was said. Declines are accepted at face value and logged; the answer 'my credit card covers it' is noted as the client's own statement and referred back to the card issuer, never assessed by the advisor.

included: a fixed offer point tied to purchase-timing mechanics
universal offering regardless of assumed buying intent
the dated offer-and-decision record and how declines are logged
excluded: assessing another product's coverage such as a credit-card benefit
recommending a specific plan to a specific traveller
re-raising the offer as a pressure tactic - the ethical rule governs that

pros.claim: A fixed offer point means nobody is skipped because the advisor guessed at their budget
pros.example: a modest-budget client who buys protection precisely because the trip's nonrefundable deposit matters more to them

pros.claim: A dated decision record answers the hardest post-disruption question in one line
pros.example: a client insisting they were never told, met with the note recording the offer, the materials sent and their decline

cons.claim: Offering to everyone in a fixed way can feel scripted to clients who have already declined before
cons.example: a repeat client asked again at the same point on their third trip and reading it as a sales routine

cons.claim: Timing the offer to purchase-window mechanics adds pressure to an early conversation
cons.example: raising protection at deposit while the client is still deciding whether to travel at all

failure_modes: deciding in advance who will not buy
offering verbally and recording nothing
letting the offer slide past the point where timing-sensitive benefit classes are still available
interpreting a client's existing credit-card or employer coverage on their behalf
acceptance_tests: every booking file shows a dated offer-and-decision record naming the product family described and the client's decision
no file shows a booking where protection was never offered without a recorded reason
revisit_triggers: the plan's purchase-timing conditions or the offer route change
a disruption exposes a file with no offer record
the requirement class for the jurisdiction changes

base.update_signal: a file surfaces without an offer record, or the product's purchase-timing conditions or offer route change

nodes.definition: Hold the conversation that makes the offer honest: map the exposure this particular trip actually creates, then point the client at the documents that decide it. The exposure map is concrete and specific to the itinerary - how much money is nonrefundable and when the penalty ladder steps up, how remote the destinations are and what medical or evacuation exposure that implies, how many connections the trip depends on, whether travelling companions' circumstances are linked, whether anyone's health history brings the look-back and purchase-timing mechanics into play, and whether the client's real worry is a named-peril cancellation or the broader cancel-for-any-reason class. What the advisor supplies is the trip's risk picture and the product's own documents; what the advisor does not supply is an interpretation of the wording, an opinion on whether a specific condition or circumstance would be covered, or any prediction of a claim outcome. The client is directed to the plan documents and the insurer or a licensed producer for those, and the referral is noted. The test of the conversation is that a client who declines still understands exactly what they are carrying themselves.

included: mapping the trip's own exposure in concrete terms
naming benefit categories and timing mechanics generically and pointing to the plan documents
recording the referral to insurer or licensed producer for interpretation
excluded: interpreting policy wording or exclusions
assessing a specific traveller's medical history or circumstances
predicting or promising a claim outcome

pros.claim: An exposure map lets the client make the decision on facts about their own trip rather than on fear or bravado
pros.example: a client seeing that most of their trip cost becomes nonrefundable on a date months before departure and deciding accordingly

pros.claim: The describe-and-refer line is protective for both sides and can be said out loud without awkwardness
pros.example: handing over the plan documents and the insurer's contact for a coverage question instead of guessing at an answer

cons.claim: Clients often want a yes-or-no answer and experience a referral as evasion
cons.example: a client asking whether a parent's condition is covered and hearing what sounds like a dodge

cons.claim: Mapping exposure well takes time on a conversation that may end in a decline
cons.example: a long fit conversation on a complex multigenerational trip where nobody buys

failure_modes: summarizing coverage in the advisor's own words and creating an expectation the plan does not carry
opining on a medical situation or a pre-existing condition
presenting the broader cancel-for-any-reason class as though it covered everything
leaving the client unable to state what they are exposed to if they decline
acceptance_tests: the file records the trip-specific exposures discussed and the documents or contacts handed to the client
no advisor-authored summary of coverage or exclusions appears in place of the plan's own documents
revisit_triggers: the trip changes materially in cost, itinerary or party composition
the product's benefit categories or timing mechanics change
a client complaint or claim shows the conversation was misunderstood

base.update_signal: a claim, complaint or regulator guidance shows the describe-and-refer line was crossed or misunderstood

nodes.definition: Bind the whole recommending surface of the practice with rules that outrank the sale. Present risk factually and proportionately, using the trip's own numbers and dates rather than catastrophe stories, because fear-selling produces purchases clients resent and reputations that do not survive a claim. Disclose compensation at the moment of recommending, not buried afterwards: that the advisor is paid when a protection plan is bought, that supplier and preferred-program relationships exist where they do, and that these relationships never decide which option is put forward first. Take deliberate extra care where a client is vulnerable - bereaved, recently diagnosed, elderly and tired, cognitively loaded, buying under pressure from a relative, or working in a second language: slow the pace, put the material in writing, invite a support person if the client wants one, and confirm understanding rather than agreement. Accept a decline the first time it is given, record it, and re-raise only if a genuinely material trip fact changes. Never trade a benefit for a review, an endorsement or a referral, and never let a compensation difference steer a recommendation without saying so.

included: compensation disclosure at the point of recommendation
the no-fear-selling standard and proportionate risk framing
vulnerable-client care and the accept-the-decline rule
the ban on traded endorsements and undisclosed steering
excluded: the compliance obligations themselves, which are named as classes in the requirement unit
product comparison and coverage interpretation
clinical or capacity assessment of any client

pros.claim: Disclosure survives contact with a bad outcome in a way that persuasion does not
pros.example: a client whose claim is denied still trusting the advisor because they were told at the outset who pays the advisor and who decides claims

pros.claim: Accepting a decline once protects the relationship that produces the next several bookings
pros.example: a client who declined protection twice still referring two households because they never felt pushed

cons.claim: Honest, unpressured selling converts fewer add-ons than fear-based selling in the short run
cons.example: a lower attachment rate than a competitor who opens with a hospital-bill anecdote

cons.claim: Compensation disclosure invites a price conversation the advisor may not want
cons.example: a client asking why they should not book direct once they learn a supplier pays the advisor

failure_modes: using catastrophe stories to close
disclosing compensation only in fine print or after the decision
re-raising a declined offer until the client relents
pressing a bereaved or overwhelmed client because the window is closing
offering an incentive in exchange for a public review or an endorsement
acceptance_tests: every recommendation that carries advisor compensation shows a contemporaneous disclosure in the client's channel of record
declines are recorded once and not re-raised in the file without a documented material change in the trip
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleges pressure, surprise about compensation or unclear framing
the practice adds an incentive, referral reward or preferred-program arrangement
a vulnerable-client situation is handled and reviewed

base.update_signal: a complaint, review or claim outcome shows a client felt pressured or uninformed about how the advisor is paid

nodes.definition: Define, before it is needed, what the advisor does when a trip goes wrong and a protection claim follows. The role is document custodian and facilitator: assemble and supply what only the advisor has - booking confirmations, supplier invoices, payment evidence, the cancellation or interruption notice, the dated timeline of what happened and when the client was told - point the client to the insurer's own claim channel and to the deadlines the plan itself states, and stay reachable while the client does the filing. The role explicitly excludes deciding whether something is covered, filling in the claim in the client's voice, characterizing a medical event, arguing coverage with an adjuster, or predicting an outcome; those belong to the insurer and, where the client wants representation, to a licensed professional. The expectation that makes this survivable was set at the sale, when the client was told plainly that the insurer decides. Commercially this is the moment the relationship is made or lost, and it also touches revenue: a plan cancelled inside its free-look window reverses the add-on commission, so the row stays provisional until then.

included: assembling and supplying the advisor-held evidence and timeline
directing the client to the insurer's claim channel and stated deadlines
holding the at-sale expectation that the insurer decides
excluded: adjudicating, arguing or predicting coverage outcomes
completing the claim on the client's behalf or in their voice
representing the client against the insurer

pros.claim: Being the fastest source of clean documentation is genuine, defensible help at the worst moment
pros.example: supplying the supplier invoice and cancellation timeline within hours while the client is still travelling home

pros.claim: A role stated at the sale keeps a denied claim from becoming a betrayal
pros.example: a client who was told at purchase that the insurer decides accepting a denial without blaming the advisor

cons.claim: The boundary can read as coldness exactly when the client is most distressed
cons.example: a bereaved client hearing a referral to the insurer's claim line as a brush-off

cons.claim: The work is unpaid and often lands during another client's active trip
cons.example: hours assembling evidence for a denial appeal in the same week two other clients are departing

failure_modes: telling a client their claim will be paid
writing the client's account of events for them
arguing coverage with an adjuster on the client's behalf
closing the add-on revenue row before the free-look window has passed
acceptance_tests: the client receives the advisor-held evidence pack and the insurer's claim channel and deadlines without any coverage opinion attached
the file shows the at-sale statement that the insurer decides claims
revisit_triggers: a claim is denied and the client disputes what was promised
an insurer changes its claim channel or documentation requirements
a free-look cancellation reverses an add-on commission

base.update_signal: a claim outcome or complaint shows the role boundary was crossed or the at-sale expectation was not set

nodes.definition: Make deliberate contact in the short window after the client comes home, while the trip is still vivid and before ordinary life closes over it. The debrief is structured rather than a courtesy note: what worked and what did not, which suppliers and guides delivered and which disappointed, what they would change next time, what surprised them, and what they are already dreaming about next. Four things come out of it. Service failures surface early enough to be addressed with the supplier and to inform whether that supplier keeps being sold. Preferences and details go into the client record while they are accurate. A review or testimonial is requested at the point of maximum goodwill. And the referral ask lands naturally, because the client is currently telling everyone they know about the trip anyway. In a vertical with no subscription and long gaps between purchases, this single unbilled hour is the cheapest source of the next booking the practice has - which is exactly why it is the first thing dropped when the advisor is busy selling.

included: the timed welcome-home contact and its structured questions
harvesting preferences, review and referral at peak goodwill
surfacing service failures for supplier feedback
excluded: service recovery and advocacy during the trip itself - trip-design and supplier-management KB
supplier selection decisions
asking for a review in exchange for anything of value

pros.claim: The contact costs an hour and produces the practice's cheapest pipeline
pros.example: a welcome-home call that surfaces a milestone anniversary trip the client had not yet started planning

pros.claim: Feedback captured warm is specific enough to act on with the supplier
pros.example: a named guide's failure reported with dates while the supplier can still investigate it

cons.claim: The debrief invites complaints the advisor must then absorb without extra revenue
cons.example: a hotel that underdelivered turning the call into an hour of advocacy after the trip has already been paid

cons.claim: It arrives when the advisor's attention has already moved to clients who are departing next
cons.example: a returning client's follow-up postponed twice during a peak departure week and then forgotten

failure_modes: sending a generic template that produces no usable information
waiting weeks until the detail has faded and the goodwill has cooled
hearing a complaint and not feeding it back to the supplier
leaving the debrief content in an inbox instead of the client record
acceptance_tests: each completed trip shows a dated debrief contact with captured notes, not just a thank-you message
each debrief records at least a preference update and an explicit review or referral outcome
revisit_triggers: a client stops booking after a trip that had no debrief
debriefs stop producing referrals or usable feedback
a supplier issue recurs across several debriefs

base.update_signal: repeat-booking or referral output from debriefed clients diverges from clients who were not debriefed

nodes.definition: Keep the client file that makes the second trip cheaper to sell and better to deliver than the first. It holds the household and the people who travel together, the dates that generate trips - anniversaries, milestone birthdays, graduations, the month this family historically starts planning - the travel-document facts the client asks to be reminded about, kept as a courtesy with the client directed to official sources for validity and entry rules, loyalty and membership numbers, seat, cabin, room, pace and dining preferences, accessibility and dietary needs, past suppliers with what happened, observed budget behaviour described as pattern rather than as a stated figure, the referral source, and the client's consent and contact preferences. Discipline runs alongside: collect what serves the client, hold it under the practice's stated privacy terms and whatever data-protection obligation classes apply in the relevant jurisdictions, keep it in the practice's own structured system rather than scattered across inboxes and phone threads, and never retain payment card details outside the supplier's own channel. This record, not the advisor's memory, is what makes a client base an asset.

included: the fields that make repeat service fast and personal
consent, retention and privacy discipline including no stored card data
keeping the record in the practice's own system rather than in inboxes
excluded: advising clients on passport, visa or entry requirements, which are referred to official sources
the trip-design use of preferences - trip-design KB
any data-protection legal conclusion, which is named as an obligation class to verify

pros.claim: A rich record turns the second engagement into a short conversation instead of a full discovery
pros.example: a repeat client's cabin, dining and pace preferences already known so the proposal arrives days sooner

pros.claim: Dates held in the record generate trips nobody had to prospect for
pros.example: a milestone anniversary recorded three years earlier prompting a timely conversation that becomes the year's largest booking

cons.claim: Every field held is a field to secure, maintain and eventually justify keeping
cons.example: accumulated health and accessibility notes that must be protected and periodically reviewed for necessity

cons.claim: Records decay quietly, and a stale preference is worse than none
cons.example: a dietary note from years ago that has changed, used confidently on a new booking

failure_modes: keeping the real client knowledge in the advisor's head or in email threads
collecting sensitive detail with no consent, retention or protection discipline
storing card data outside the supplier's channel
never refreshing preferences after a debrief
acceptance_tests: a repeat client's record shows household, key dates, preferences, past suppliers, referral source and contact consent, updated at the last debrief
no payment card data is held by the practice and every retained sensitive field has a stated reason and retention position
revisit_triggers: a client updates household, health or accessibility circumstances
consent or contact preferences change
the practice changes systems or the applicable data-protection obligation class changes

base.update_signal: a client's circumstances or consent change, or the practice changes the system or jurisdiction in which records are held

nodes.definition: Build the calendar that keeps a low-frequency practice present without becoming noise. The cadence is anchored on the client's own dates rather than on the advisor's marketing calendar: the anniversary of the trip, when memory and appetite peak together; the celebration dates in the record; the month this household has historically started planning; and the season when their kind of destination is actually decided. To that is added event-driven contact that is genuinely relevant to the recorded pattern - a route or ship that fits what they said they wanted, a destination they once called a someday trip. The mechanic that decides whether this works is timing: reach the client before their planning window opens, because a client who has already been browsing has usually anchored on a price and a shape of trip, and the advisor is then arguing rather than designing. Frequency is disciplined, every message carries something the client can use, consent and opt-out are honoured immediately, and the practice tracks which anchors actually produce conversations rather than sending because the calendar said so.

included: anchoring contact on client dates and historic planning windows
relevance-tested event-driven touches
frequency discipline, consent and opt-out honouring
excluded: broadcast marketing strategy and lead generation - agency-models KB territory for positioning
designing the trip that results - trip-design KB
re-raising a declined protection offer as a cadence touch

pros.claim: Contact timed before the planning window catches the client while the trip is still shapeable
pros.example: reaching a family in the month they historically start planning, before they have priced a package online

pros.claim: Anchoring on the client's own dates makes routine contact feel personal rather than promotional
pros.example: an anniversary-of-the-trip note recalling a specific moment from their itinerary, which reliably restarts the conversation

cons.claim: Cadence decays into noise the moment relevance drops, and unsubscribes are hard to reverse
cons.example: a generic seasonal promotion sent to a client whose recorded pattern makes it obviously irrelevant

cons.claim: Maintaining a per-client calendar is real ongoing work in a practice with no spare hours
cons.example: a peak season in which the cadence is skipped entirely and the following year's pipeline thins

failure_modes: sending on the advisor's calendar rather than the client's
reaching out only when the advisor needs bookings
ignoring an opt-out or a request for less contact
treating every client as having the same travel rhythm
acceptance_tests: each active client record carries at least one date-anchored next contact derived from their own history
every cadence message can be justified as useful to that specific client, and opt-outs are actioned immediately
revisit_triggers: response rates fall for an anchor type
a client asks for less contact or opts out
a client's life stage or travel rhythm visibly changes

base.update_signal: engagement with an anchor type changes across a cycle, or clients begin asking for reduced contact

nodes.definition: Treat referral as a designed act rather than a hope. The ask happens at the moment of maximum satisfaction, which in this business is the welcome-home debrief or the moment a disruption was handled well, and it is specific rather than generic: naming the kind of traveller and trip the practice serves best gives the client something they can actually match a friend against. The handoff is made easy - a short forwardable introduction that says what the practice does, who it is for, and how engagement works including that planning is done under written terms, so a referred prospect arrives informed instead of surprised. The loop is then closed: the referrer hears that the introduction landed and, later, that the trip went well, which is what produces the second referral. Ethics are load-bearing here. Any incentive that exists is disclosed to both sides, nothing of value is exchanged for a public review or an implied endorsement the client does not hold, and a client who does not want to refer is never asked twice. Referral source is recorded so the practice can see where its book actually comes from.

included: the timed, specific ask and the forwardable handoff
closing the loop with the referrer
disclosure of incentives and recording referral source
excluded: paid lead generation and advertising
trading value for reviews or endorsements
the niche and positioning statement itself - agency-models KB

pros.claim: A specific ask produces matchable introductions where a generic one produces goodwill and nothing else
pros.example: asking who in their circle is planning a milestone anniversary rather than asking them to keep the advisor in mind

pros.claim: Closing the loop converts one referrer into a repeat source
pros.example: telling a referrer their friend's trip went well, which brings a second introduction within the season

cons.claim: Asking can make a warm relationship feel transactional if it is mistimed or repeated
cons.example: a referral request arriving while a client is still unhappy about a supplier failure

cons.claim: Referred prospects arrive with expectations set by someone who does not know how the practice works
cons.example: a referred enquirer surprised by written engagement terms because the referrer described the service as free

failure_modes: asking generically and getting nothing
asking a client whose trip had an unresolved problem
offering an undisclosed incentive or trading a benefit for a review
never telling the referrer what happened
failing to record where a client actually came from
acceptance_tests: referral asks are recorded with their timing and the forwardable material used
every incentive in use is disclosed to both parties and no benefit is exchanged for a review or endorsement
revisit_triggers: referral volume changes materially
referred prospects consistently arrive with mismatched expectations
an incentive or partnership arrangement is introduced or changed

base.update_signal: referral volume or the quality of referred enquiries shifts, or an incentive arrangement changes

nodes.definition: Decide what to do about the quiet majority of a client base, which in this vertical is most of it at any moment. Dormancy is defined against each household's own rhythm rather than a fixed number of months, because a family that travels every second or third year is not dormant at month thirteen while a twice-yearly cruiser might be. Segments follow: likely to return on their normal interval, life-stage changed in a way that pauses or reshapes travel, lost to a competitor or to booking direct, and never really a client at all. Each segment gets a different act - the first gets timing, the second gets patience and a changed conversation, the third gets one honest attempt to learn why and to offer a reason to come back, the fourth gets retired from the calendar. Reactivation contact is useful rather than pleading: something relevant to what the record says they wanted. Retirement is real housekeeping - opt-outs honoured, records minimized to what the practice can justify keeping - and the outcome of every triage is written back to the record so the book's true size is honest rather than flattering.

included: dormancy measured against the household's own interval
segmentation into return, changed, lost and never-a-client
one honest reactivation attempt and honest retirement of records
excluded: discount-driven win-back campaigns and price-cutting
pressure contact after an opt-out
acquisition of new clients, which is not this KB's subject

pros.claim: Rhythm-relative dormancy stops the practice writing off clients who are simply between trips
pros.example: a biennial traveller left alone at the point a fixed twelve-month rule would have declared them lost

pros.claim: An honest triage tells the advisor how big the book really is
pros.example: a list of several hundred names resolving into a much smaller set of households who actually travel with the practice

cons.claim: Reactivation attempts often confirm a loss the advisor would rather not know about
cons.example: learning that a long-standing client has been booking direct for two years

cons.claim: Segmenting on thin evidence can retire a client who was about to return
cons.example: a household paused by an illness being retired from the calendar just before they start planning again

failure_modes: applying a single fixed dormancy interval to every household
treating silence as a decision without one honest contact
repeated contact after an opt-out
keeping a flattering headline client count that nobody believes
acceptance_tests: each dormant record carries a segment, the interval it was judged against, and the outcome of any reactivation contact
retired records show opt-out honoured and retention reduced to what the practice can justify
